source.title: Annotation Guidelines: Clinical Trial Cohort Selection
source.author: Amber Stubbs

chronology: Use the most recent original record date as the evaluation date, regardless of its calendar year.
The annotation guide assumes a patient's status persists between records until a subsequent record indicates a change.
A historical event must fall within the criterion's required interval, rather than merely being mentioned in a recent record.
A record header provides document context. Preserve any separate event date, correction, uncertainty, explicit denial, or retrospective statement.

criteria.text: History of intra abdominal surgery, small or large intestine resection or small bowel obstruction

Advanced cardiovascular disease. For the purposes of this annotation, we define "advanced" as having two or more of the following: Taking two or more medications to treat CAD; History of myocardial infarction; Currently experiencing angina; Ischemia, past or present
Current alcohol use over weekly recommended limits
Use of aspirin to prevent myocardial infarction
Serum creatinine > upper limit of normal
Taken a dietary supplement (excluding Vitamin D) in the past 2 months
Diagnosis of ketoacidosis in the past year

Major diabetes-related complication. For the purposes of this annotation, we define "major complication" (as opposed to "minor complication") as any of the following that are a result of (or strongly correlated with) uncontrolled diabetes: Amputation; Kidney damage; Skin conditions; Retinopathy; nephropathy; neuropathy
Patient must make their own medical decisions
Myocardial infarction in the past 6 months

scoringOnly.statement: These binary sensitivities are applied after prediction freeze. They do not establish why clinical evidence was unknown.
